item.title: Weakened association between sequential phenological events corresponds to interphase extension
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79161-w

Seasonal events in temperate deciduous trees, from leaf-out to leaf fall, follow a fixed annual sequence. This study shows that the timing of consecutive events is statistically associated in European trees, but that the association between fruiting and leaf coloration has weakened in some species as the interval between these phases has increased.

item.title: Hydrogen-bond-mediated quasi-two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks for ultrahigh gold extraction
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78532-7

Covalent organic frameworks are ideal for precious metal recovery but the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer and limits extraction capacities. Here, the authors report a quasi-2D topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery.

item.title: A combinatorial genetics approach reveals limits to redundancy within Plasmodium falciparum invasion ligand families
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 30 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78985-w

The authors use a genetic approach to explore redundancy within two multigene families important for Plasmodium falciparum invasion of human red blood cells, revealing that not all family members function equivalently.
